title: Sanitation and hygiene
summary: How to wash hands, mix and use bleach solutions safely, site latrines and bucket toilets away from water, and handle greywater, waste, dead animals, rodents and insects. It also covers keeping drinking water separate from everything else.

steps.text: Wash hands with soap and water for 20 seconds at the key times. Use sanitiser only as a backup.
Read the bleach label for its percentage, find your row in the bleach table, and mix fresh each day.
steps.warn: Never mix bleach with ammonia, vinegar, acids or any other cleaner. The gas is toxic.

steps.text: Dig toilets at least 30 m from any water source and keep waste, greywater and drinking water apart.
Cover waste, bag dead animals, seal food and empty standing water to keep rodents and insects away.

notes:
## Call first

**If help can be reached, call it first.** Call your poison centre or 9-1-1 if bleach is swallowed or fumes make breathing hard (CDC, CRC). Ask your local health authority how to dispose of waste and dead animals (CDC). If no help is coming, see [When no help is coming](#ref/reference_sanitation/when_no_help_is_coming).

## Handwashing

1. Wet hands with clean running water, turn the tap off, add soap.
2. Lather the backs, between fingers and under nails.
3. Scrub **20 seconds or more**, rinse, dry on a clean towel (CDC). The Canadian Red Cross teaches at least 30 s (CRC).

Wash before and after preparing food, eating, caring for someone sick, and treating a wound. Wash after the toilet, changing nappies, coughing or sneezing, touching animals or animal waste, and touching garbage (CDC).

**Sanitiser limits:** use at least 60 % alcohol, only when soap and water are not available. It works poorly on visibly dirty or greasy hands, does not remove chemicals such as pesticides or heavy metals, and does not work well on norovirus. Avoid homemade recipes (CDC).

## Bleach solutions

Use plain unscented bleach. Read the label: it should say 5 % to 9 % sodium hypochlorite. Do not use "splashless", colour-safe or stronger bleach with these recipes (CDC).

| Use | Target | 5 to 6 % bleach, per 1 L of mix | 8.25 % bleach, per 1 L of mix | Keep wet |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Taps, handles, seats, floors | 600 to 800 ppm | 12 mL (2½ tsp) | 8 mL (1½ tsp) | 2 min (WA DOH) |
| Sick household, toilets | 1,000 ppm | 20 mL (4 tsp) at 5 %; 17 mL at 6 %* | 12 mL* | 5 to 10 min (CDC) |
| Faeces, vomit, after wiping up | 5,000 ppm | 100 mL at 5 % (1 part bleach, 9 water); 83 mL at 6 %* | 61 mL* | 10 min (PHO) |

*Calculated, not from a table: bleach mL per litre = 1,000 x target % / bleach %. Rows 2 and 3 at 5 % are from Health Canada and PHO.

- Food surfaces and dishes, after washing: 5 mL (1 tsp) bleach in 750 mL water, then rinse (Health Canada).
- Clean off dirt with soap and water first (WA DOH).
- Pour bleach into cool water. Make it fresh each day. Label the bottle (Health Canada, CDC).
- Wear gloves and eye protection. Open windows (CDC). Never use bleach on skin (Health Canada).
- **Never mix bleach with ammonia, vinegar or other acids, or any cleaner.** The gas is toxic (Health Canada).
- **Laundry:** gloves, do not shake. Wipe stool off with toilet paper. Hottest water, detergent, longest cycle, hot dry. Bleach may go in the rinse. Bag heavily soiled items you cannot clean (CDC).

## Latrines and distances

| What | Minimum |
|---|---|
| Toilet from groundwater source or well | 30 m (100 ft) (UNHCR/Sphere, King County) |
| Toilet from surface water, home or camp | 30 m (100 ft) (King County) |
| Pit bottom above groundwater | 1.5 m (UNHCR/Sphere) |
| Untreated greywater from a well or bore | 50 m (WHO EMRO) |

Keep drinking sources upstream. Never defecate on banks of streams or ponds used for water, or on crops (WHO). Local rules may be stricter.

**Trench latrine:** 0.2 to 0.3 m wide, 1.5 m deep, 4 m long. Cover waste with soil daily. Close it when waste is 0.3 m from the surface (WHO).

## Bucket toilet

1. Line a 19 L (5 gal) pail, or a toilet bowl, with **two** heavy garbage bags. Put cat litter, ash or sawdust in the bottom (King County).
2. Keep the lid closed (King County).
3. Each day tie the bags and store them in a protected place until disposal is safe: working sewer or septic, buried on your own land, or garbage service if authorities allow (King County).
4. Handwashing beside it: soap, water, paper towels. Keep it away from food areas (King County).

## Flushing with a bucket

When the taps stop but the drains still work, a toilet flushes if you pour water straight into the bowl. Pour about 4.5 L (1.2 US gal) quickly, from 30 to 60 cm (1 to 2 ft) up, so the rush starts the siphon (ACWD). Use water you wouldn't drink (Alberta water shortages).

It only helps if the waste can flow away:
- **Septic tank and field with no pump (all gravity):** keeps working with the power off (Texas A&M AgriLife).
- **Septic with a pump or other powered parts:** waste collects in the system while the power is out, and the reserve can be small. Texas sets the minimum at a third of a day's design flow, about 300 L (80 US gal) for a three-bedroom house. For an outage of less than a day, use water only for flushing and hand-washing; for a longer one, or once drains run slowly, stop all water use (Texas A&M AgriLife). Then use a [bucket toilet](#ref/reference_sanitation/bucket_toilet).
- **Town sewer with lift stations:** many have only an alarm and no backup power, so their storage fills fast and sewage can back up into basements. Flush only for solids, pour no wash water or other liquids down any drain or toilet, run no laundry or dishwasher, and keep use low for about an hour after the power returns. A closed backflow valve keeps the sewer out, but your own water can then back up inside (West Hants).
- **Upper floors with a blocked drain below:** water sent down the drains will likely end up in the basement or lower levels (Roxborough Water). Stop using water until the blockage is cleared: see [Sewer backup](#guides/safety_sewer_backup).

## Greywater

Greywater is bath, shower, basin and laundry water. It carries faecal bacteria. Kitchen and toilet water are not greywater (WHO EMRO).

- Avoid contact. Do not store it. Keep it off vegetables (WHO EMRO).
- Use only what the soil can take up. Keep it 1.5 m above groundwater (WHO EMRO).
- Keep bloody or heavily soiled laundry out of it (WHO EMRO).

## Dead animals, vermin and insects

- **Human waste:** keep it out of water and food first (WHO).
- **Dead animals:** waterproof gloves, boots, eye protection. Small: bag turned inside out over your gloved hand. Large: shovel into a bag. Wash hands, disinfect boots and clothes, shower (CDC).
- **Human remains:** bodies of people killed by injury, drowning or fire do not cause epidemics. Bodies of people who died of an infectious disease can be infectious: handle them as little as possible, with gloves, boots and eye protection, and wash hands. Leaking bodies can foul water (PAHO).
- **Rodents:** remove food, water and shelter. Keep food in tight lids. Air out a closed space for 30 minutes before cleaning up droppings, wet them with bleach solution rather than sweeping, and wear an N95 or better mask in confined spaces (CDC, Health Canada).
- **Droppings:** air out 30 min, gloves on, spray with 1 part bleach to 9 water until wet, wait 5 to 10 min. **Do not sweep or vacuum.** Wipe, double-bag (CDC, Health Canada).
- **Mosquitoes:** once a week empty or cover standing water. Use screens and repellent (CDC).
- **Flies and other insects:** cover waste with soil or a lid (WHO, King County).

## Keep drinking water separate

- Store drinking water in clean, covered containers (EPA). Label wash and bleach buckets "NOT FOR DRINKING" (CDC).
- Cloudy water: settle and filter. Rolling boil for 1 minute, at least 2 minutes above 2,000 m (6,500 ft) (Health Canada BWA).
- Or add 2 drops of unscented 5 to 9 % bleach per 1 L, stir, wait 30 min. Double if cloudy (Health Canada, EPA). Below 10 °C (50 °F), double it and wait 1 to 2 hours (HealthLinkBC 49b). Boiling does not remove chemicals (EPA).

## When no help is coming

**Human waste**
- Short stay: a cat hole 15 to 20 cm (6 to 8 in) deep, 60 m (200 ft) from water, trails and camp. Cover it. Pack out toilet paper (NPS).
- Longer stay: a trench 0.2 to 0.3 m wide, 1.5 m deep, 4 m long. Cover waste with soil daily and close it at 0.3 m from the top (WHO). Or a pit at least 0.9 m (3 ft) deep, with soil, ash or lime after each use (King County).
- Keep either 30 m (100 ft) from wells, springs, streams and homes (King County, UNHCR/Sphere). Put the base at least 1.5 m above the water table (UNHCR/Sphere); King County's own minimum is only 0.3 m (1 ft) above the water table or hard pan (King County). Never on stream banks or crops (WHO).

**The dead**
- Bodies of people killed by injury, drowning or fire do not cause epidemics. Do not hurry or mass-bury. Lime spray does nothing (WHO/PAHO manual).
- Wear gloves and boots, and wash hands with soap after (WHO/PAHO manual). If the cause was infectious disease such as cholera, add a mask, eye protection and overalls, seal the body in a watertight bag or plastic sheet, keep relatives from touching it, skip ritual washing, and bury near where the person died with few people present (WHO TN8).
- Record first: a unique number on waterproof labels on body and wrapping; photos of face, whole body and marks with the number visible; sex, approximate age, belongings, where and when found (WHO/PAHO manual, WHO TN8).
- Burial: 1.5 m deep, one layer, 0.4 m apart, 200 m from streams, lakes, springs and (for 4 or fewer bodies) wells. Base 1.2 m above the water table (1.5 m in sand), or 2 m if you can (WHO TN8). Mark and map each grave (WHO/PAHO manual).

**Bleach poisoning**
- Swallowed: rinse the mouth (NNEPC), sip water (Ontario Poison Centre). Do not induce vomiting. No fluids if vomiting, drowsy or struggling to swallow (MedlinePlus bleach).
- Eyes: lukewarm water for at least 15 minutes (Ontario Poison Centre). Skin: wash at once, remove clothing (NNEPC).
- Fumes: fresh air. Breathing still hard after that is serious (Ontario Poison Centre).
- Serious: strong bleach, a big swallow, drooling, burns, bloody vomit. Damage can continue for weeks (NNEPC, MedlinePlus bleach).
